PullRequest.Title: agentHost: hosts enable multipleChatProviders during initialize instead of after a reconnect
PullRequest.Body:
Lets a VS Code client tell an Agent Host about `chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled` during `initialize`, so turning multi-harness on no longer forces a reconnect. The default stays off; turning it on in Insiders is a follow-up once a published host includes this.

- With the setting on, the client sets `_meta['vscode.multipleChatProviders']` in `initialize`, and the host turns its gate on before answering, so the handshake already advertises `multipleChatProviders`. Previously the client re-initialized each remote connection (closing its transport) once its mirrored setting reached the host: an SSH host without an SSH config host can't reconnect, and a Dev Container connection lost the authentication in flight.
- The flag follows the same rules as a client `RootConfigChanged` setting the property: it is ignored on unauthenticated and passive relay lanes, and while the property is read-only or owned by the extension's root config overlay.
- Hosts that ignore the flag behave as before (the client re-initializes once).

Builds on #347377 (experiment-controlled settings).

### Validation

- eslint, hygiene, `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js'`: 17720 passing, 75 pending (includes a regression test for direct and relay lanes)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Enabling the client setting on a remote host forced one redundant full transport reconnect after the initial handshake. That repeated the remote connection and initialize round trip and could fan out restoration work across cached credentials and active subscription snapshots before the client became usable with the capability.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Remote agent-host connection readiness was delayed by an avoidable reconnect, with interruption and retry of in-flight subscription work; environments that could not recreate the transport could fail to recover at all.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: A client whose multiple-chat-providers setting is already enabled requests the gate in its first initialize; the host enables it before forming the response, eliminating the replacement transport, duplicate initialize, authentication restoration, and subscription snapshot restoration from connection startup.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, when the mirrored host gate became true after the first handshake, `_maybeReinitializeForChatProviders` set `_freshInitializeRequested`, cleared transport listeners, and routed closure through reconnect. The reconnect path constructs and connects a replacement transport, sends a fresh `initialize` with all current subscription URIs, restores authentication, and requests snapshots for active subscriptions omitted from the handshake. The existing regression test also demonstrates an in-flight subscribe being interrupted and retried on the replacement transport. The added initialize metadata at browser/agentHostProtocolClient.ts:1615 plus the server-side pre-response gate update at node/protocolServerHandler.ts:1085 makes the first handshake advertise the capability, so that reconnect branch is not entered on current hosts.

Scenarios.Scenario: First direct remote Agent Host connection with multiple chat providers enabled and a cold/off host gate
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The client opens the transport and sends `initialize`; the host synchronously updates root state before creating the response, after which the first response already advertises the capability. The queued host-config filesystem persistence is not awaited and is off the handshake critical path. Before the PR, the first handshake completed without the capability, config mirroring enabled the gate, and the client then closed the transport and required a replacement transport plus another initialize before capability-ready progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial Agent Host transport connection and initialize request/response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialize round trip per connection; metadata adds one boolean field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial transport and initialize occurred, but the response could omit the capability.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for connection readiness both before and after the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize root config, mkdir, write temporary config, and rename
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued write when the cold gate changes from off to on; subsequent connections see the enabled value and skip the update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The client's post-handshake mirrored `RootConfigChanged` performed the same root-config persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued on `_rootConfigWrite` without awaiting it, so it is off the initialize response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replacement transport connect, duplicate initialize, credential restoration, and subscription snapshot restoration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the PR, one replacement connection and initialize per affected client, authentication work per cached credential, and snapshot work per active subscription omitted from initialize; after the PR, zero on a current host for this startup gate transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The client deliberately cleared the transport listeners and entered fresh-initialize reconnect after receiving the mirrored host gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously blocked capability-ready connection and interrupted in-flight work; removed by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Credential count and active session/chat/other subscription count controlled the old reconnect restoration cost; the new metadata itself is constant size. Root-config observers may scan loaded sessions once, but that same gate transition occurred through post-handshake mirroring before the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The initialize handler and root-state mutation run synchronously. The config write is serialized by `_rootConfigWrite`. Authentication restores in parallel except for Web PubSub relay, and subscription snapshots restore sessions first then chat/other groups in parallel, but that entire old burst is avoided.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The host root value is the effective positive cache. Cold/off performs one update; warm/on makes `enableMultipleChatProviders` a no-op. There is no negative-cache retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed metadata reaches the initialize handler, the gate is set before `_supportsMultipleChatProviders` forms the result, and the old reconnect/restore call path is directly present and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual network latency and counts of active credentials/subscriptions vary by remote environment, but the removed replacement transport and duplicate initialize are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; this is a concrete repeated-work latency fix and was recorded with `report_regression_fix`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Authenticated, non-passive relay connection with the setting enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initialize metadata crosses the relay; only a relay lane with confirmed authentication can enable the host gate before the response. The same constant-time gate check and root-state update apply; asynchronous persistence remains off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request/response per relay connection; one boolean metadata property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initialize already crossed the relay, then allowed config mirroring could trigger a later reconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The gate decision is synchronous before the response; no additional relay round trip is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the enabled host root setting
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for the cold gate transition across concurrent clients because the first synchronous update makes later checks observe true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An allowed client root-config action persisted the same gate after the handshake.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneous relay clients; effective mutation cardinality remains one per off-to-on host transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Relay authentication status gates the mutation. JavaScript synchronous mutation coalesces concurrent initialize arrivals through the updated root value; filesystem writes are sequenced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm enabled hosts skip mutation and persistence. Unknown authentication is treated as ineligible, not retried by this code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from `_mayClientEnableMultipleChatProviders`, synchronous root-state update, and the no-op enabled check.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Relay RTT varies, but the PR adds no additional round trip and can remove the prior reconnect.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; authorized relay startup avoids repeated connection work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unauthenticated or passive relay, restricted relay-root host, extension-owned/read-only gate, or setting disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The client either omits the metadata when disabled or the server rejects its ability to mutate the gate before any root-state update. Initialize proceeds through the existing handshake path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialize occurred without this metadata-driven gate path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new boundary work; only local metadata/property checks occur.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Connection count only; each connection performs constant-time eligibility checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent connection handling; no shared write is scheduled because the eligibility check fails or metadata is absent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache mutation and no persistence. Existing client compatibility/reinitialize behavior remains for hosts or lanes that cannot accept the flag.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the explicit early-false conditions and conditional client metadata.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the performance conclusion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; disallowed/disabled paths add only constant-time checks and no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Warm/local host or older host compatibility
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A warm/local current host already seeded with the gate returns the capability immediately; `enableMultipleChatProviders` observes true and does no state or filesystem work. An older host ignores the unknown metadata and follows the pre-existing mirror/reinitialize fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize against a current warm host or older compatible host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normal initialize; an older host may still incur the pre-existing one-time reconnect fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Warm local hosts already advertised the capability from environment seeding; older hosts used the mirror/reinitialize path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Current warm hosts add no work; older-host behavior is unchanged because unknown metadata is ignored.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One connection; metadata size is constant and does not scale with sessions or subscriptions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No added shared work on warm current hosts. Older-host reconnect concurrency is pre-existing and bounded to at most once per client gate cycle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive root-state cache avoids mutation on warm hosts. Compatibility relies on older hosts ignoring unknown `_meta` fields; no negative cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the guarded setter and existing at-most-once reconnect guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Older-host deployment prevalence is unknown, but their performance behavior is not worsened.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and the initialization, config propagation, persistence, reconnect, authentication, and subscription restoration paths. No diff-introduced performance issue was found. The PR removes a proven redundant remote reconnect and its scaling restoration work; that regression fix was recorded against commit 8c18263e1c0837d1e2df1fb63409ee18da07a970.
